eligibility.quote: The bug is due to the different Kobuki plugins using the same ImuSensor.
eligibility.reason: E1/E4: the multi-robot reproducer and maintainer diagnosis document wrong odometry. E2: separately instantiated plugins resolve a shared sensor registry incorrectly only with another model present. The repair changes the code's sensor reference to a fully scoped identifier, not merely a launch/configuration binding. E3: CONCURRENT matches the reported two-model failure. Eligibility stands, although exclusive ownership is not the supported interface interpretation.

failed_conditions.quote: Hence, the sensor obtained by `sensors::SensorManager::Instance()->GetSensor()` is subject to a race condition.
failed_conditions.reason: The documented defect is ambiguous name resolution selecting another model's readable sensor. The sources do not establish an exclusive claim, incompatible ownership requests, or a sensor that cannot be shared. Each robot needs the correct sensor identity, not exclusive access to a common sensor. Class other is supported; resource:imu still identifies the implicated registry object.

loudness.quote: KGP does not post rotations to the odom topic (translations are there)
loudness.reason: The documented symptom is missing rotational data while models move; no build/connect/activation diagnostic is supplied. silent_documented is supported.

detection_stage.quote: KGP catches these and moves around properly in gazebo world
detection_stage.reason: The discrepancy is observed during simulated movement: run.

resolution.quote: I have confirmed that it resolves #38. Thanks @slivingston!!!
resolution.reason: The confirmation is explicitly attached to the single-change PR for the two-instance reproducer. Both selected units are instances of that same patched plugin, so the PR identifies their common resolved code. observed is supported without having to infer a separately released peer's version.

notes: Read the initial 15 of 18 issue timeline entries exposed by GitHub HTML, PR #39 comments, and its patch. The issue tail was not independently retrieved; the PR supplies the direct resolution confirmation. The preliminary setEuler/setRPY change was explicitly reported insufficient and concerns orientation construction rather than the selected inter-instance sensor lookup. Similar unscoped bumper/cliff lookups are not evidence that those sensors failed in this case.
